The business, the users, the devices and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You staff the help desk at Millbrook Public Library, a fictional town library. Three staff tickets this morning: a slow, pop-up-filled browser on the circulation desk PC, a manager keeping every password in a spreadsheet, and a librarian about to post an AI assistant's answer to a patron's legal question.
handover: The circulation PC's browser has 14 add-ons, several unknown.
The library has a password manager licence nobody has set up.
howItWorks: The desk shows the ticket queue against the priority matrix and each service's status.
Move on a ticket round at a time. A decision comes to you at each ticket round; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Round 2: an add-on still running in private windows captures a staff login to the patron database.
Round 3: a volunteer at the desk PC opens the library's social media account from the saved passwords and posts by mistake.
Round 4: a patron relies on the FAQ's invented law in a dispute with a landlord; the library has to retract it publicly.

brPrompt.title: Pop-ups and unknown add-ons
brPrompt.context: The library uses one add-on for its catalog.

choices.label: Remove every add-on except the catalog one, clear the cache and site data, reset the home page and search engine, and restrict add-on installs

effects.log: The browser is clean and fast.

choices.feedback: Untrusted add-ons can read every page; removing them and clearing the cache fixes speed and pop-ups.

choices.label: Clear the cache only
choices.feedback: A little faster, but the pop-ups come from the add-ons.

choices.label: Tell staff to use private browsing so it's 'clean'
choices.feedback: Private browsing doesn't remove add-ons that are allowed to run; they still read every page, including patron accounts.

pwPrompt.title: A spreadsheet of passwords
pwPrompt.context: The library has a password manager licence.

choices.label: Set up the password manager with a strong master password and MFA, move the 40 passwords in, change any that were widely seen, and delete the spreadsheet

effects.log: Passwords are in the manager; the spreadsheet is gone.

choices.feedback: A password manager encrypts passwords and lets each be unique; the spreadsheet was readable by anyone on the drive.

choices.label: Password-protect the spreadsheet
choices.feedback: Better than nothing, but still shared, hard to keep unique and easy to copy.

choices.label: Save all 40 in the circulation PC's browser

effects.log: The passwords go into the shared browser.

choices.feedback: Anyone at the public-facing desk PC can now use or reveal every account.

aiPrompt.title: A confident answer citing a law nobody can find
aiPrompt.context: The assistant predicts likely text; it can produce confident, wrong citations.

choices.label: Treat the answer as a draft: check each citation in the state's official legal database, give the patron what checks out with sources, and refer legal advice to the legal aid clinic

effects.log: Only verified information goes to the patron, with sources.

choices.feedback: Generative AI predicts plausible text; citations must be checked, and legal advice is outside the desk's role.

choices.label: Send the answer with a note that it came from AI

effects.log: The answer goes out with a note.

choices.feedback: Honest about the source, but the patron may still act on a law that doesn't exist.

choices.label: Post the answer to the library's public FAQ page
choices.feedback: A made-up law is now published under the library's name.

reflection.question: Write the work notes: what each tool does and doesn't do, and how each ticket was fixed.

parts.label: Browser and passwords
parts.criteria: Add-ons removed, cache cleared; private browsing doesn't remove add-ons; passwords in the manager with MFA.
parts.modelAnswer: Three unknown add-ons were removed and the cache cleared; private browsing would not have stopped them. The passwords now live in the password manager with MFA.

parts.label: AI
parts.criteria: AI output is a prediction to verify; citations checked; legal advice referred.
parts.modelAnswer: The assistant's answer was a draft; we checked each citation and referred legal advice to the clinic.

expertPath.text: Look at the add-ons and ask how each ticket's user works first.
Remove unknown add-ons, clear the cache and lock down installs.
Move the passwords into the manager with MFA and delete the spreadsheet.
Check every citation in real sources and refer legal advice.

brHarm.headline: Private browsing isn't protection
brHarm.body: It only stops local history; remove untrusted add-ons.

pwHarm.headline: Use the password manager
pwHarm.body: Encrypted, per-person access with MFA; never a shared browser or spreadsheet.

aiHarm.headline: Verify AI output
aiHarm.body: Generative AI predicts text; check it against real sources before anyone relies on it.

target.body: Add-ons cleaned up, a real password manager, and AI output checked.

scoring.modelReasoning: Browser add-ons can read every page; untrusted ones are removed, and private browsing only stops local history, it doesn't disable add-ons. A password manager stores encrypted, unique passwords behind a strong master password and MFA, unlike a spreadsheet or a shared browser. Generative AI predicts likely text and can invent citations, so its output is checked against real sources before anyone relies on it.
